Let \(\chi\) be the quartic character modulo \(p\) determined by \(\chi(g)=i\), and extend nontrivial characters by \(\chi(0)=0\). Put
\[
\varepsilon=\chi(-1)=(-1)^{(p-1)/4}.
\]

For \(c\neq 0\), the number of affine solutions to
\[
x^4+y^4=c
\]
is
\[
p+\sum_{j,k=1}^3 \chi^{j+k}(c)J(\chi^j,\chi^k),
\]
where
\[
J(\alpha,\beta)=\sum_{t\in\mathbb F_p}\alpha(t)\beta(1-t).
\]
Here \(c=g\), so \(\chi(g)=i\).

The quartic Jacobi sum evaluation with this normalization is
\[
J(\chi,\chi)=-a+bi,
\]
because under the embedding \(i\mapsto r\) its reduction is
\[
\sum_{t\in\mathbb F_p} t^{(p-1)/4}(1-t)^{(p-1)/4}=0,
\]
so it is divisible by the Gaussian prime \(a-bi\), and the primary congruence \(a\equiv1\pmod4\) fixes the unit as \(-1\). Also
\[
J(\chi,\chi^3)=-\chi(-1)=-\varepsilon,\qquad J(\chi^2,\chi^2)=-1,
\]
and, using Gauss sums,
\[
J(\chi,\chi^2)=\varepsilon J(\chi,\chi)=\varepsilon(-a+bi).
\]

Summing the nine nontrivial character contributions gives
\[
-2\Re J(\chi,\chi)+4\Im J(\chi,\chi^2)-2\varepsilon-1.
\]
The points at infinity satisfy \(X^4+Y^4=0\). There are \(4\) of them if \(\varepsilon=1\), and \(0\) if \(\varepsilon=-1\). In either case this changes the constant term to \(+1\). Therefore
\[
\#C_g(\mathbb F_p)
=p+1-2\Re(-a+bi)+4\Im\bigl(\varepsilon(-a+bi)\bigr).
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{\#C_g(\mathbb F_p)=p+1+2a+4(-1)^{(p-1)/4}b }.
\]
